items.title: Edwards closes Sunday, and it is the one in-metro device seat
items.detail: Six of your 17 open rows close in the six days from Wednesday, October 28 to Sunday, November 1, and only three of them are in your metros: Analysis Group Health Care (Los Angeles, Wednesday), Gilead's Oncology Biomarker AI seat (Foster City, Friday, genomics so it ranks last) and Edwards Clinical & Regulatory (Irvine, Sunday). The page still shows no ticks and no applications added by hand, so it cannot tell whether any has gone out. Edwards is the harder one to leave: it is a device company, it lists statistics as an eligible degree, it offers conversion into new grad programs, and it closes on a weekend, so Friday is the real deadline. If a send is stuck on a cover letter, one paragraph is enough for Edwards. Tick each row on the page once it goes out.

items.title: The next two weeks
items.detail:
**By Wednesday, October 28:** Analysis Group Health Care, the strongest consulting fit here: resume, unofficial transcripts and a cover letter naming Los Angeles. The posting says review continues after the deadline, so a late send is not dead.

**By Friday, October 30:** Edwards Clinical & Regulatory (Irvine; the form closes Sunday). The same day, Merck Outcomes Research and J&J Oncology Epidemiology close, both in the Northeast.

**October 31:** Merck Biostatistics (Rahway, New Jersey).

**By November 13:** J&J Statistics & Decision Sciences (La Jolla or virtual). Write to Mackenzie Mueller (see Contacts) before you send it.

**No close date shown:** Boston Scientific Graduate Clinical Insights Research Intern (urology real-world evidence, Maple Grove). It names your degree and your May 2028 graduation window, so it is worth sending early even though it is in Minnesota.

**Remote, until January 8:** J&J Global Market Access. Lead with the health economics side of your work; it can wait until the October dates are done.

items.title: How this field hires a master's student
items.detail: Big pharma opens structured summer programs between September and November and often prefers or requires a PhD for biostatistics seats; read the qualification line before the title. Gilead's October 16 batch listed PhD as *preferred* on most statistics reqs and still took master's students; its research AI seats that remain are omics and lab work. Contract research organizations hire master's statisticians at volume, but later and more rolling, and mostly in SAS. Southern California device companies run their own calendars: Stryker and Edwards' clinical track are open now; Medtronic's master's window closed October 13. Health plans posted a wave at the end of September, mostly undergraduate, MBA or pharmacy seats. J&J posts batches with short windows and sometimes moves them: its Oncology Epidemiology seat was re-posted October 16 with the close pushed a week to October 30.

items.title: J&J: Statistics & Decision Sciences Intern
items.location: La Jolla (San Diego) or virtual; also New Jersey, Pennsylvania
items.detail: J&J Innovative Medicine's statistics group, inside Global Development. Requires *pursuing an MS, PhD, or equivalent graduate degree in Statistics, Biostatistics*, Data Science or related, 3.0 GPA, 10 to 12 weeks May to August 2027; preferred *R, Python, or related tools*. Projects run from discovery through Phase 2 and 3 trials: data preparation, visualization, modeling, simulations to optimize study designs, and building software that supports statistical analyses, where your R Shiny app fits. La Jolla is one of four sites and the posting says *Virtual internships are potentially available*; hybrid, housing stipend possible, $23.50 to $52.50 an hour. Interns are evaluated for *potential for future employment*. Posted October 13. A Michigan alum did this internship in 2025; see Contacts. Req R-103411. [Apply](https://jj.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/JJ/job/Raritan-New-Jersey-United-States-of-America/Statistics---Decision-Sciences-Summer-Interns-2027_R-103411)

items.title: Analysis Group: Summer Analyst, Health Care
items.detail: Names *first year masters/MPH candidates* in biostatistics or epidemiology. Claims, EHR and trial data in R, SAS and Stata; cost-effectiveness and budget-impact models. $2,000 a week, 3.3 GPA floor, evaluated for a full-time offer in your internship office. Deadline Wednesday October 28, interviews begin in November, then rolling review; re-read October 26; the posting says rolling review continues after the deadline. items.title: How to get the offer
items.detail: Say in week one that you want a return offer and ask what earns one; ship something that outlives the summer; meet people on adjacent teams.

sections.title: What this page ranks against
sections.note: If any of this is wrong, say so and the ranking changes.

items.title: Private industry first: pharma, CROs, biotech
items.detail: Hospital systems and research institutes are fine; no government or public sector. Public universities and their hospitals are excluded; private nonprofits like Kaiser, Cedars-Sinai, City of Hope and Mayo are in.

items.title: Clinical trials, devices, health analytics
items.detail: Genomics stays on the map but ranks last.

items.title: Consulting: scientific yes, strategy no
items.detail: HEOR, epidemiology and economic consulting count (Analysis Group, Exponent). Strategy and management consulting does not (Guidehouse; ZS is out on that rule).

items.title: MS Biostatistics, Michigan, May 2028
items.detail: Master's only. BS Data Science and Anthropology, ASU, 4.0, Barrett Honors.

items.title: R and Python strong, SQL moderate, SAS in progress
items.detail: Also Tableau, R Shiny, ggplot2, scikit-learn; XGBoost recurrence model (AUC 0.75), SARIMA influenza capstone. Open question: **when does the SAS class end?** Reqs that say *SAS and/or R* are open to you now.

items.title: LA, Orange County, Bay Area, San Diego, Phoenix, remote
items.detail: Six rows outside these metros sit near the end of Open now (New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Texas, Michigan); say if they should come off. Humana's Graduate Analytics Internship fits your degree but is on-site in Louisville or five hubs outside your metros, so it sits in Not a fit until you say otherwise. Actuarial is on your title list; the first actuarial seats this cycle wanted a passed exam or an undergraduate, so say if you plan to sit an exam.
